--- title: "Build a design matrix" subtitle: "Model event timing with a typed spec and inspect the regressors." jupyter: python3 --- ## Create Events ::: {#b247eb6e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd import fmrimod as fm from fmrimod.spec import hrf, compile as compile_spec from fmrimod.design_colmap import design_colmap events = pd.DataFrame({ "onset": [0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40], "condition": ["face", "scene", "face", "scene", "face", "scene"], "response_time": [0.8, 1.1, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0, 1.2], "duration": 2.0, }) events ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
onset condition response_time duration
0 0 face 0.8 2.0
1 8 scene 1.1 2.0
2 16 face 0.7 2.0
3 24 scene 0.9 2.0
4 32 face 1.0 2.0
5 40 scene 1.2 2.0
``` ::: ::: ## Define the Acquisition Grid ::: {#e82f1915 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} sf = fm.SamplingFrame(blocklens=60, TR=1.0) sf.samples[:8] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` array([0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5, 6.5, 7.5]) ``` ::: ::: ## Build the Design from a Typed Spec `hrf(...)` is a typed value. `compile()` lowers a spec against the events and sampling frame into an `EventModel` (and its baseline) — no fitting, no string formula. The design matrix and column metadata are inspectable immediately. ::: {#f5297d2a .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} spec = hrf("condition", basis="spmg1") event_model, baseline_model = compile_spec(spec, data=events, sampling_frame=sf) event_model.design_matrix.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (60, 2) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#df08b9c6 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} event_model.column_names ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['condition_condition.face', 'condition_condition.scene'] ``` ::: ::: ## Inspect Column Metadata `design_colmap` reports the provenance of every column — which condition, which basis, what role — for the compiled event model. ::: {#0b3baa03 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} design_colmap(event_model)[["col", "name", "condition", "role", "basis_name"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
col name condition role basis_name
0 1 condition_condition.face condition.face task SPMG1
1 2 condition_condition.scene condition.scene task SPMG1
``` ::: ::: ## Add a Parametric Modulator To model a condition modulated by a trial-by-trial continuous variable (reaction time, accuracy, confidence, ...), use the typed-spec `modulators=` keyword. This expands the term into an unmodulated boxcar plus one regressor per modulator. By default each modulator is mean-centered at the raw-value level (pre-convolution), giving the unmodulated boxcar and modulated columns the near-orthogonal structure that makes per-modulator betas interpretable. ::: {#0b027318 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} modulated_spec = hrf("condition", basis="spmg1", modulators=("response_time",)) mod_model, _ = compile_spec(modulated_spec, data=events, sampling_frame=sf) design_colmap(mod_model)[["col", "name", "condition", "role", "basis_name"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
col name condition role basis_name
0 1 condition_condition.face condition.face task SPMG1
1 2 condition_condition.scene condition.scene task SPMG1
2 3 condition_response_time_condition:response_time_1 condition:response_time_1 task SPMG1
3 4 condition_response_time_condition:response_time_2 condition:response_time_2 task SPMG1
``` ::: ::: The added `response_time` regressors appear as their own columns, tagged with where they came from. Because the modulator is part of the typed term metadata rather than a formula-string suffix, you can read off exactly which column belongs to which term before fitting anything. To see a design like this carried through `fmri_lm`, a contrast, and into a group analysis, follow the **[golden path](golden-path.qmd)**. See the [parametric modulators](parametric-modulators.qmd) tutorial for the full story on centering semantics, the `center_modulators=` opt-out, and why fmrimod does not orthogonalize modulators automatically. ## Next - [The golden path](golden-path.qmd) — the whole workflow into group, with a parity check - [Linear model](linear-model.qmd) - [Contrasts](contrasts.qmd) - [Overview and workflow](overview-workflow.qmd)
